The Oxford takes its name from Oxford University — the style originated in Scotland and Ireland in the early 1800s and quickly caught on among university students. These lace-up dress shoes are clean, classic, and traditional. The “cap toe” refers quite literally to the toe box and the seam sewn on the leather there. Originally meant to reinforce the area, it became a visual statement of the shoe’s formality — cap-toe dress shoes are the most formal option in a man’s wardrobe and are well-suited to white-tie or black-tie events. Ours are made in Italy from soft, supple calf leather. They feature durable Goodyear construction, wherein the upper is stitched to the outsole, and leather soles and lining. The stacked wooden heel has a rubber top lift for traction; note the gentleman’s notch at the heel, a design element meant to minimize the chance of it catching on the cuff of your trousers.

The Guardian 2 Selvedge is a 14.25oz Japanese selvedge denim developed with an emphasis on strength and long-term durability. The fabric blends cotton with Kevlar®, an aramid fiber developed in 1965 and best known for its exceptional tensile strength, meaning its resistance to tearing and being pulled apart.
An interesting fact about Kevlar® is that its discovery was accidental. It was originally developed while researchers were trying to create a lightweight reinforcement fiber for tires. Instead, they produced a fiber so strong and stable that it went on to be used in body armor, aerospace components, and high-performance industrial applications.
Unlike performance fabrics that abandon traditional denim character, Guardian 2 retains the look, feel, and aging potential of classic selvedge denim while offering significantly higher tear resistance than a 100% cotton equivalent. While the jeans are not bulletproof, the Kevlar® content dramatically improves durability in high-stress situations and repeated wear.

Our relaxed tapered cut jeans, made from 19oz left-hand twill selvedge denim. While most of our denim features a traditional right-hand twill weave — characterised by a diagonal grain running from the top-right to the bottom-left of the fabric — this “lefty” denim is woven in the opposite direction under very high tension. This creates one of our stiffest, most robust fabrics, with an intense indigo hue that tends to fade with higher contrast than looser weaves.
To create this darkened variation, we take a pair of standard IH-888S-19L jeans and steep the entire garment in black dye using a direct dyeing process. This stains the indigo denim and stitching, with the added bonus of removing all shrinkage from the fabric. A unique middle ground between our traditional indigo and black denims, over time the fabric will gradually fade with blue-tinged hues in high-wear areas.

In our very early Wythe development, we knew we wanted to have a core bedford cord program - we had found so many vintage garments worn by cattlemen and ranchers in the 40s and 50s and the fabric spoke to us in a way that just felt right. These vintage pants were so broken in, so soft, yet still managed to feel bulletproof. We loved how it broke in and knew this was going to be a staple of ours. And while the five-pocket pattern from Wythe has gone through many different stages of fit and fabrication, we've now settled on a level of consistency across our different fabrics that we're very happy with.
This particular bedford cord is just what we were looking for in a workwear staple. It's woven on vintage selvedge loom by a Japanese mill that specializes in weaving this fabric, exactly like it used to be made in the 40s and 50s. It's one of the only fabrics this mill produces.
One of the amazing things about bedford cord is how hard wearing it is on the outside, but how soft and stretchy it is on the inside. It breaks in and molds to your body like raw denim, and is easy to see why this was a favored fabric for workwear.

We've used Selvedge denim in a variety of pieces over the years, but we're adding another style to that list with our Selvedge Denim Baseball Hat Series.
"Selvedge" denim gets its name from the self-edge finish on either edge of the fabric that prevents fraying and unravelling. This self-fabric edge is most commonly referred to as "selvedge." It's a mark of quality and can be quickly identified by a signature stripe that runs along a seam or cuff in a garment. These stripes are usually seen at a cuffed pant leg or at the top edge of a coin pocket. Although subtle, once you're aware of it, you'll start to notice it and the range of colors that these stripes come in. This stripe can vary but traditionally it's a white stripe with a red line running through it.
Our Dehen 1920 baseball hats now include the iconic selvedge stripe as a subtle detail on the adjustable strap. This combination of Redline Natural Selvedge Bull Denim crown and Indigo Sashi-Ori brim and button creates the most unique hat we've ever created!

The Daytripper was originally thought up once we got our hands on a 1940s "austerity" British Battledress. We had been delving into 1960s Laurel Canyon culture (and more notably, the counterculture), Woodstock, Ken Kesey and his followers, etc. We really appreciated how these people wore and styled militaria. They were taking these masculine symbols of war and flipping them on their heads- they'd cut them up, repurpose them, decorate them with their own DIY patches and embroideries, and really change how these garments were viewed, and changed what they represented.
We felt this jacket was a great way to do that in our own way. We played on the theater-made insignia that you'd often see on a lot of military garments and made our own for the Daytripper. We used our cotton/linen slub twill that you find on our chinos and Officer's Shirts and applied it to the multi-pleated, cropped body of the battledress. Best worn open over our ringer tees.
